title: A latent control model for realistic rodent motion
abstract: arXiv:2610.27279v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The development of embodied models of animal behavior is a major goal of the neuro-AI community. Embodied models will enhance our ability to make direct comparisons between biological and artificial agents. To make such comparisons effective, though, we need embodied models that actually move like animals. Previous work has developed virtual animal bodies and techniques for training realistic motion through imitation. However, to date, there is no system for embodied animal modeling that produces natural movements both during trained goal-directed behavior, and during exploration driven by random generation. translated_title: 一种用于逼真啮齿动物运动的潜在控制模型
translated_abstract: 开发动物行为的具身模型是神经-AI领域的一个重要目标。具身模型将增强我们对生物智能体和人工智能体进行直接比较的能力。然而，要使这种比较有效，我们需要真正像动物一样运动的具身模型。先前的工作已经开发了虚拟动物身体以及通过模仿学习训练逼真运动的技术。然而，迄今为止，还没有一个具身动物建模系统能够既在经过训练的目标导向行为中，又在由随机生成驱动的探索过程中产生自然的运动。在这里，我们介绍了SCAMPER（通过增强运动先验实现具身强化学习模拟控制），这是一个训练具身虚拟大鼠模型的系统，能够在目标导向行为和随机探索过程中都实现自然的运动。SCAMPER使用一种具有两种不同先验的变分架构，即一种用于……的运动先验
tldr: 提出了SCAMPER系统，利用具有双重先验的变分架构训练具身虚拟大鼠模型，使其在目标导向行为和随机探索中都能产生自然的运动，弥补了以往具身动物建模的不足。
en_tdlr: SCAMPER introduces a variational architecture with dual priors to train an embodied virtual rat model that produces natural movements during both goal-directed behavior and random exploration, filling a gap in embodied animal modeling.
